insight: Specs over data modules in `desktop/src` are stub-passable whenever the expected value is read back out of the module under test (`toBe(profile.cliInstall.unix)`), so catalog contents must be asserted as literal strings.

Functions in `desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` that take `&AppHandle` to read `app.path()` cannot be exercised by any spec because `tauri` is declared with `features = []` in Cargo.toml (no `test` feature, so no `mock_app`), so a plan that asserts resolution-order behavior must require the candidate directory list be injectable — otherwise the specs silently degrade into testing an array the test itself built.

The desktop package's `pnpm test` covers only pure logic (`test/rules.test.ts`, `test/catalog.test.ts`) and vite.config has no jsdom/happy-dom environment, so any plan touching `desktop/src/main.ts` or `desktop/index.html` must add a manual verification step — a UI control can be deleted with every gate green.

The Tauri config sets `"csp": null` and main.ts builds several elements via `innerHTML`, so any new `#[tauri::command]` that accepts a free-form string and executes it (shell, path, URL) hands the webview that authority directly — prefer commands that take an identifier and resolve the dangerous value Rust-side.

The test Active Storage service is Disk rooted at `tmp/storage` with no teardown anywhere in `test/test_helper.rb`, so objects survive between suite runs — any spec asserting "uploaded once" or "not present" must generate fresh per-run content or it passes on the first run and fails (or falsely passes) on the next.

This codebase's append-only pattern (`def readonly? = persisted?`, as in Activity) makes `has_many ..., dependent: :destroy` raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord when the parent is destroyed — append-only children must cascade via `dependent: :delete_all` or the FK.

A worktree branch created from `origin/main` tracks it; with `push.default=upstream` a bare `git push -u origin <branch>` fast-forwards main itself — set push.default=simple repo-wide and unset the stale upstream before any worker pushes.

Any new table carrying both workspace_id and a parent id (channel_id, agent_session_id, agent_run_id) must get a composite foreign key `column: [<parent>_id, workspace_id], primary_key: [id, workspace_id]` in addition to the plain FK — this is the database-level guard that a child of one workspace cannot reference a parent of another, established in 20260801130001_workspace_id_everywhere.rb and carried by all 5 existing room tables, and adding workspace_id to Workspace::Boundary::ROOMS alone does not provide it.

Cards i174/i176/i177/i179 were all critic-rejected on the same shape: specs exercised the plan's new seams (struct-literal agents, free functions, rendered strings) but not the production entry point (launch, commands, bridge actions) — a PLAN must state which production path each spec drives, or the second critic round will reject it.

In desktop/src/main.ts every promise started without being awaited carries an explicit `.catch` (silent `() => {}` for telemetry, `alert(String(err))` for user-facing work), so any new callback handed to api.ts must terminate its own rejection rather than relying on a caller to await it.

The client opens `channels[0]` (`desktop/src/main.ts:865`) and the API returns `Channel.order(:name)` (`server/app/controllers/api/v1/channels_controller.rb:7`), so any seed or preview data meant to be seen on a fresh install must live in the alphabetically first channel — `marketing`, not `meetings`.

`bin/preview` can be run against a throwaway database without disturbing a developer's server on :3000 by exporting `VITE_WORKROOM_SERVER` (baked in by the build it runs), `WORKROOM_SERVER`, `WORKROOM_PREVIEW_PORT` and `WORKROOM_SHOTS` and pointing a second `bin/rails server` at a `DATABASE_URL` of its own — `DATABASE_URL` overrides the `database:` key in `config/database.yml`.

Every channel-child table carries a composite `(channel_id, workspace_id)` foreign key to `channels(id, workspace_id)` that is NO ACTION, and Postgres enforces it before the plain `channel_id` key, so `on_delete: :cascade` on the plain key never fires — the Rails `dependent:` option is the only cascade, and dropping it breaks channel deletion outright.

`Api::V1::BaseController` already wraps every request in `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction` via `around_action :within_one_transaction`, so a controller-level rollback spec passes with or without an explicit inner transaction block and cannot on its own evidence that the action wraps anything.

`bin/preview` can be pointed at any server without touching the development database by exporting `WORKROOM_SERVER`, `VITE_WORKROOM_SERVER` (the client reads it at build time, and `bin/preview` builds the client itself), `WORKROOM_PREVIEW_PORT` and `WORKROOM_SHOTS` against a Rails server started with a scratch `DATABASE_URL`.

The test object store is Active Storage Disk under `server/tmp/storage` with no teardown, so any spec using fixed fixture content finds the object already stored before the request meant to store it — content-addressed specs must randomize their bytes (e.g. `SecureRandom.hex`) or they pass vacuously.

All `.flow` worktrees share one PostgreSQL test database, so running `bin/rails test` from a worktree whose `db/schema.rb` predates another's migration silently downgrades the schema for every worktree (`unknown attribute 'sha256' for Artifact`); `bin/rails db:test:prepare` in the newer tree restores it.

A Minitest fixture helper named `message` overrides Minitest's own `message` method, so every assertion that has to build a failure message raises instead of reporting — name message fixtures `posted`/`said` instead.

Only `messages_controller#create` appends `message.created`; `runs_controller#message` creates agent-authored messages without journaling, so every `message.created` envelope carries MessageSerializer's User branch (with email) and a fixture journaling an agent message would spec a shape the product never produces.
`Memory::Store.current=` pins a process-wide store that `current` never un-resolves, so any spec that swaps the seam must reset it to nil in teardown or the whole suite becomes order-dependent.
